=== 1. Izumo — the 韓国伊太弖 knot. There are THREE, not two. ===

''You asked for the sources to be read, not just the graph: "it is best to look over the source page [[:ja:出雲国の式内社一覧|出雲国の式内社一覧]] and the kokugakuin shrine database things here." Done 2026-08-19. The earlier report reasoned from Wikidata alone — its Kokugakuin column was literally blank — and it was wrong.''

'''意宇郡 has three 同社坐韓国伊[大太]弖神社 entries, in three different precincts:'''

! entry !! register name !! host precinct !! Wikidata !! Kokugakuin id
|-
| '''19''' || 同社坐韓国伊'''太'''弖神社 || 玉作湯神社 || [[d:Q135040778|Q135040778]] || 182793
|-

: '''✓ 2026-08-19 (bot):''' Entry '''19''' was missing from the old report entirely, and it already has its own item. So "one item standing in for two entries" was one entry short. Ordinals verified by counting the template independently — 48 entries, matching its own header (意宇郡 48座) — not taken on trust from the graph.
: Two things the sources say that Wikidata does not:
:* jawiki's identified modern shrine for entry '''28''' is spelled 韓国伊'''太'''弖神社 — 太, not 大. The old report leaned on 大/太 as the thing separating the two entries. The register names differ that way; the modern identifications do not.
:* The Kokugakuin ids run in step with the ordinals but '''skip 28 and 39''': 18→182792, 19→182793, 20→182794; 27→182801, 29→182802; 38→182811, 40→182812. Entry 19 got a page of its own; 28 and 39 did not.
: '''→ 2026-08-19, checked against the database — and my guess was WRONG.''' I had proposed that entries 28 and 39 live as ''sections'' of their host shrine's Kokugakuin page. They do not.
:* [https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=182793 182793] is a page for '''同社坐韓国伊太弖神社''' in its own right — so a 同社坐 entry '''does''' get its own page when it has one.
:* [https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=182801 182801] (揖夜神社, entry 27) and [https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=182811 182811] (佐久多神社, entry 38) contain '''no 同社坐 mention at all'''.
: So entries '''28 and 39 are simply absent from the database'''. Their ids do not exist — there is nothing to qualify, and no section to add. The missing-id set for them is real.

'''What P958 actually is''' — established the same day, and it changes item 3 more than it changes this one:

: '''One Kokugakuin page = one 927 register entry.''' The page lists that entry's 論社 as numbered blocks — <code>現社名など（１）（２）（３）…</code> — and '''P958 is which numbered candidate the item is'''. Examples with many:
:* [https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=181186 181186] 火地神社 — 10 candidates; §1 is 火地神社（多気郡岩内村）, matching the page's （１）.
:* [https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=181177 181177] 相鹿木大御神社 — 9.
:* [https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=181688 181688] 石楠尾神社 — 7.
: That is why <code>0</code> and <code>n/a</code> carry no uniqueness: they mean “not one of the numbered candidates”.

'''The under-specification, measured.''' Across all '''900''' Kokugakuin ids held by more than one item: 619 fine, '''281 wrong'''. '''197''' have a holder with no section while its siblings have one (page 181621's shape — so that page was not unusual), 66 have no sections at all, 18 are all <code>0</code>/<code>n/a</code>. '''Nothing collides''': nowhere do two items claim the same (id, real section), so the fault is always a missing value, never a contested one. Browsable: https://emmaleonhart.github.io/shintowiki-scripts/p958-candidates.html

: '''Open, and it is a METHOD question not a shrine question:''' 321 items are missing a section. Only 57 can be derived from a parent's ranking; '''228 have nothing in Wikidata to derive from'''. But since P958 is just the page's candidate index, matching an item's name against the numbered list should recover it — on a 12-page sample that matched '''40 of 46 (86%)'''. The six misses were mostly spelling variants (関山神社 vs 關山神社（上越市）) rather than wrong sections.
: '''ASK:''' run that match across all 228 and hand you the confident ones separately from the judgement calls?

=== 2. The duplicated "part of" statements — ANSWERED 2026-08-19 ===

''Your note was: "I am not sure what is going on here. But I think it is resolved. Not being as strong as claiming it 'is' resolved." You were right to hedge — it is not resolved, and the shape is not what the old "22 duplicates" line said.''

: '''✓ 2026-08-19 (bot):''' 116 item/list pairs carry more than one <code>part of</code> into the same 神名帳 list. Split by ordinal:
:* '''14''' — the same ordinal repeated. The real defect.
:* '''47''' — '''distinct ordinals. LEGITIMATE, do not touch.''' One shrine covering two register entries — the 坐韓国伊大弖神社 shape from item 1.
:* '''55''' — one side carries no ordinal.
: Worst is tangled rather than doubled: [[d:Q110915859|Q110915859]] holds ordinals 20, 34, 16, 20, 34, 5, 14 into one list.

'''The question was whether an unqualified <code>part of</code> is always the leftover to strip. Checked against the list side — and the answer is NO.'''

{| class="wikitable"
! of the 55 !! what the list itself says !! what that means
|-
| '''42''' || the list names this item '''nowhere''' || removing the blank fixes nothing — it just deletes one of two claims the list never confirmed either way
|-
| '''10''' || names it at exactly the ordinal we already carry || '''the blank really is a leftover''' — safe to strip
|-
| '''2''' || does not confirm the ordinalled side || unresolved
|-
| '''1''' || names an ordinal the item '''does not carry''' || a different repair entirely — an add, not a removal
|}

: So a blanket "strip the unqualified ones" would have been wrong for '''45 of 55'''. Only the 10 are safe on this evidence. Full per-item data, all three classes, is committed at <code>modern-quickstatements/p361_multi_part_of_audit.json</code> so the 47 legitimate ones are recorded and a later pass cannot "clean" them.
: '''ASK:''' the '''42''' where the list names the shrine nowhere are the same shape as the orphan problem in item 3 — an item claiming a membership the list does not reciprocate. Should they be worked as part of that, rather than as a duplicate-statement cleanup?
